items.title: Avenda Health adds intraoperative Surgery Mode to Unfold AI
items.excerpt: Avenda Health added an intraoperative Surgery Mode to Unfold AI, letting surgeons use AI-generated prostate cancer maps built from a patient's MRI, biopsy and other data during procedures.

items.title: AI leads to lower turnaround times for high-volume imaging
items.excerpt: A study found AI use lowered report turnaround times for high-volume imaging, and that most AI-related latency came from data routing rather than the algorithms themselves.

items.title: AI on par with radiologists for finding prostate cancer on MRI
items.excerpt: A study of 22,445 prostate MRI exams from 21,252 men in 22 countries found an AI system matched radiologists in detecting clinically significant prostate cancer (Radiology).

items.title: FDA clears Elucid's new AI-enabled FFR-CT software
items.excerpt: FDA cleared Elucid's FFR-IQ, AI software that estimates fractional flow reserve from coronary CT angiography using coronary anatomy and plaque composition to guide treatment decisions.

items.title: CT tool may detect pulmonary fibrosis progression more than 2 years sooner
items.excerpt: Artificial intelligence-powered quantitative CT analysis is capable of identifying signs of pulmonary fibrosis months before clinical diagnosis, according to a new multicenter study.

items.title: FDA Official Believes GenAI-enabled Tools Will Need to Be Assessed Like a Physician
items.excerpt: Rick Abramson, a radiologist by training and the director of FDA's Digital Health Center of Excellence said, "We ended up putting out this idea that maybe these devices are starting to behave a little bit more like me as a physician than a heart valve or a defibrillator."

items.title: AMA Calls for Risk-Based GenAI Oversight to Protect Patients and Support Responsible Innovation
items.excerpt: As generative AI moves toward performing increasingly consequential clinical functions, the American Medical Association (AMA) is urging the U.S. Food and Drug Administration to address a foundational question: Who is responsible for ensuring that these tools remain safe once they enter clinical practice?

items.title: Epic launches Connectors to link its AI tools with third-party apps
items.excerpt: Epic launched a new capability that lets its artificial intelligence agents access information and perform tasks in third-party applications. | Through "Connectors," developers can connect their apps to Epic's AI tools—Emmie, Art and Penny—as well as custom AI agents organizations create through Agent Factory.

items.title: Before the ambulance arrives: How AI is helping the NHS rethink patient care
items.excerpt: Yorkshire Ambulance Service NHS Trust is using AI for planning, training and call analysis before crews reach patients, as the NHS rethinks pre-hospital emergency care.

items.title: Why this startup is taking its AI to predict breast cancer risk directly to patients
items.excerpt: A startup didn't want to wait for doctors and insurers to get behind its breast-cancer risk prediction AI. So it's going directly to patients.

items.title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Mental Health Care
items.excerpt: A JAMA Psychiatry Viewpoint calls for community-wide coordination to evaluate large language models before and during their use in mental health care.

items.title: Multimodal Machine Learning-Based Prediction of Relapse in Major Depressive Disorder
items.excerpt: A multimodal machine learning model predicts relapse risk in patients with major depressive disorder, aiming at early identification for personalized preventive strategies.

items.title: Agentic Automation of BT-RADS Scoring Using an End-to-End System for Standardized Glioma Follow-up
items.excerpt: An end-to-end multiagent LLM and CNN system automates Brain Tumor Reporting and Data System (BT-RADS) scoring of posttreatment glioma MRI, integrating imaging trends, medication effects and radiation timing.

items.title: Can commercial artificial intelligence replace onsite cytopathologists for rapid onsite evaluation during EUS-guided tissue acquisition?
items.excerpt: Rapid onsite evaluation (ROSE) by a cytopathologist improves EUS biopsy yield but is not universally available due to workforce shortages; this study tests whether commercial deep-learning AI can stand in for the onsite cytopathologist.

items.title: AI-Assisted Molecular Review Refines SMO Inhibitor Candidacy in SHH Medulloblastoma
items.excerpt: An NEJM AI case study shows AI-assisted molecular review refining which patients with SHH-subgroup medulloblastoma are candidates for SMO inhibitor therapy.

items.title: Comprehensive or Wasteful? Clinical AI and the Up-front Workup
items.excerpt: An NEJM AI editorial examines whether clinical AI tools that recommend extensive up-front diagnostic workups make care more comprehensive or more wasteful.
